summary.verdict: The U-9 check DID repeat the §3 error. It checked whether a matching product exists in the Catalog, not whether the specific merchant's listing exists. For 7 non-Shopify merchants (carparts.com, evasivemotorsports.com, fitmentindustries.com, autobarn.net, turbokits.com, bcracing-na.com, hardmotion.com), their products CANNOT be in the Shopify Catalog. The matching products found were from other Shopify merchants selling the same or similar products.
summary.restatedU9Conclusion: The U-9 conclusion 'all 18 are present in the Catalog API' should be restated as: 'All 18 product queries returned results in the Catalog API, but 7 of the 18 cited merchants are non-Shopify and therefore cannot have listings in the Catalog. The matching products came from other Shopify merchants. For the 11 Shopify merchants, 3 are verified present (scan set) and 8 are likely present but not verified at seller level.'

implications: The U-9 verdict of INCONCLUSIVE (same-index evidence) is weakened. The Catalog API does not contain non-Shopify merchants' listings, yet those merchants appear in assistant results. This means the assistants draw from a broader index than the Catalog API.
This is consistent with §2.2: a diagnostic built only on Catalog data measures a partial competitive field.
Set B still cannot be assembled from these 18 candidates — the 7 non-Shopify merchants can't have shop.app listings either.
The 8 unverified Shopify merchants would need seller-level Catalog checks to confirm their own listings are present.
